newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African races differ over govt, Mandela --survey.
newsitem.headline: S.African races differ over govt, Mandela --survey.

text.p: South Africa's race groups have sharply divergent opinions on President Nelson Mandela and his government, a new survey has found.
Results of the study released on Monday showed 77 percent of blacks applauded Mandela's performance as president, slightly down from last year's 85 percent.
Only three in 10 whites rated him as good to very good, down from the four to five last year. The biggest group of white opinion (42 percent) was that Mandela was putting in an average performance.
Forty-one percent of mixed-race coloureds said he was good or very good in the job and around 37 percent of South Africans of Asian origin said the same.
The government was given lower marks by the 2,500 people polled in the survey, which has been carried out in April for the past three years.
Sixty percent of blacks, by far the largest group in South Africa's estimated 37.9 million population, rated the government's performance as good to very good, down from last year's 67 percent.

"Compared to six in 10 blacks, less than one in 10 whites and under two in 10 coloureds or Indians thought the government was performing well," said Hanna Fourie, managing director of survey company Market Research Africa, who carried out the study for Business Day newspaper.

"The white majority view (55 percent) was that the government was performing poorly, 41 percent of Indians agreed, while 42 percent of Indians and just over half of the country's coloureds believed it was average."
